review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for uses of the `pullbackIsoProdSubtype_*` and `pullbackFst`/`pullbackSnd` lemmas. The composition forms `pullbackIsoProdSubtype_inv_fst` and `pullbackIsoProdSubtype_inv_snd` carry `@[simp]`. Their pointwise forms do not. Downstream files (OpenImmersion, TopComparison, Gluing) pass the pointwise lemmas by hand. I did not run Lean, so I did not check whether simp already closes these goals by another route. The orientation of the proposed lemmas, with a pullback projection applied to `.inv` on the left and a subtype projection on the right, strictly simplifies, so I see no loop risk. I did not recommend `@[simp]` on `pullbackIsoProdSubtype_hom_apply`, because it would expand the pullback into an anonymous-constructor subtype element. I also did not recommend it on `pullbackFst_apply` and `pullbackSnd_apply`, because I found no downstream uses that show a need.

findings.excerpt:
pullback.fst f g ((pullbackIsoProdSubtype f g).inv x) = (x : X × Y).fst :=
  congr($(pullbackIsoProdSubtype_inv_fst f g) x)
findings.problem: The composition forms `pullbackIsoProdSubtype_inv_fst` and `pullbackIsoProdSubtype_inv_snd` are `@[simp]`, but their pointwise forms are not. Simp normalizes `(a ≫ b) x` to `b (a x)`, so the composition lemmas do not fire on `pullback.fst f g ((pullbackIsoProdSubtype f g).inv x)`. The simp set therefore has no rule for the normal form that elements actually take. Downstream code works around this by naming the lemmas by hand. OpenImmersion.lean lists them as extra simp arguments. TopComparison.lean and Gluing.lean, and this file itself, use them in `rw`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `pullbackIsoProdSubtype_inv_fst_apply` and `pullbackIsoProdSubtype_inv_snd_apply` with `@[simp]`. The rewrite is terminating and moves toward the canonical form, because `pullback.fst`/`snd` of an inverse-iso image becomes a plain `Prod.fst`/`Prod.snd` of the underlying subtype element. Callers could then drop the explicit lemma arguments in `simpa [...]`, as in OpenImmersion.lean lines 324-325.
findings.benefit: The simp set becomes complete for elements of the pullback. Proofs about points of `pullback f g` stop needing manual `rw` or explicit simp-argument lists, and the simp attributes on the composition forms and the pointwise forms become consistent.
